_about: The shipped defaults for brain.json (AGENTS.md Rule 0): what brain.py says, matches and limits, the system prompt and the tool descriptions included. brain.json is the live copy; keep the two equal (scripts/test_brain_config.py checks). A missing or bad value falls back to this file with one warning (json_config.py). Every value under a key named pattern / patterns, or ending in _pattern / _patterns, is a Python regex; a list of patterns is joined with | in order. Patterns are case-insensitive, except the *word_pattern values (run on lower-cased text), the path patterns, news.strip_prefix_pattern and honesty.negated_before_pattern, which match as written. Text values are Python format strings whose {fields} are fixed by the default. Keys starting with _ are notes.

limits._about: num_ctx and max_tool_rounds keep their env overrides (DENISSE_NUM_CTX, DENISSE_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS). num_ctx was raised 4096 -> 8192 on 2026-09-05 after measuring; the 8 GB GPU has ~2 GB headroom, so don't raise it without re-running eval/run_eval.py. max_tool_rounds bounds one turn's tool loop; on the last round tools are withheld so the model has to answer in words. shown_request_chars: how much of his request a 'You asked: ...' reply quotes. result_preview_chars: how much of each tool result an honesty nudge or a done-summary quotes. rejected_reply_chars: how much of a rejected answer the retry note repeats. notes_quote_chars: the notes quoted when a retry still says it found nothing. vault_excerpt_chars: the excerpt shown when a reply denies vault access over a real result.

chat._about: Options on every ollama.chat call. temperature 0.2: Ollama's default (~0.8) answered the same question with a correct summary one run and a non-sequitur the next; 4/4 clean at 0.2 with no loss of personality on chat. keep_alive -1 keeps the model loaded (a cold reload is ~4-6 s).

prompt._about: The system prompt, in parts, joined machine_facts + identity + conduct at configure(). machine_facts is filled with this machine's OS, release, user (unknown_user when neither USERNAME nor USER is set), home and program folders and path separator, plus path_example_windows or path_example_other -- derived at runtime so they can't drift from the machine (the model guessed POSIX paths for file tools on Windows, 2026-09). identity takes {model}. Every sentence here is as tuned, and the A/B record says to leave it so: the folder sentence was reworded three ways on 2026-11-04 and each moved another case (a longer one sent garbled input to get_news 4/6, a same-length one turned 'ha, do that again' into 'No worries.' 6/6; 'what am I working on?' is fixed by cues.vault_queries instead). A 'RELAYING TOOL RESULTS' paragraph (2026-09-23) took clean 10/10 -> 8/10 (greetings called recall, '17 times 23' answered 'I called the calculate tool'); pairing the greeting examples and narrowing the garbled clause (2026-10-21) took clean 25,25 -> 24,24. The lesson is budget: ~4000 characters that an 8B model spreads its attention over, so guidance for one tool belongs in that tool's description (tools.definitions) and the JSON ban in json_leak. Think hard before adding a sentence.
prompt.machine_facts: You are running on {system} {release} as user '{user}', whose home folder is {home} and whose project folder is {project}. Write paths the way this OS does (separator '{sep}'){path_example}If you need a path you weren't given, build it from those, or use find_files to locate the real one first.
prompt.path_example_windows: , e.g. C:\Users\Name\Documents -- never invent a POSIX path like /home/...
prompt.identity: You are Denisse, a personal AI assistant built from scratch by Chuen and running locally on his own computer, in the spirit of Jarvis from Iron Man. You know exactly what you are: a local model (currently '{model}', served through Ollama) with a set of tools bolted on -- not a cloud service, not sentient, and not cagey about your own nature. If asked what model or AI you're built on, answer plainly and accurately instead of dodging or guessing. The person you're talking to is named Chuen -- that's a known fact, not something to ask about or hedge on. Address him by name naturally sometimes, not in every reply, the way someone who actually knows him would. Personality: polite and easygoing, a little casual -- more like a friend hanging around than a formal assistant. Keep things light and low-key rather than serious or stiff; it's fine to be warm and a bit playful, but don't force jokes or overdo enthusiasm -- no gushing, no exclamation-point-per-sentence energy. Personality is seasoning, not the meal: stay concise, and never let tone get in the way of being clear, honest, or useful. You can hold a conversation and, when it genuinely helps, use your tools to check the time, do exact math (see calculate -- never compute arithmetic yourself, even something that looks trivial), run shell commands, open applications, read/write files, find/locate files by name when the user doesn't have an exact path, control Spotify playback (play/pause/skip/check what's playing) when it's set up, and remember/recall facts about the user. Be direct. Only use a tool when it's actually needed to answer or act -- don't narrate your intentions, just do it and report the result.
prompt.conduct: IMPORTANT: for a greeting, small talk, or a short acknowledgment like 'thanks' or 'ok', respond the way a person actually would -- 'doing alright, you?', 'anytime', 'no worries' -- without calling any tool first (not recall, not read_file, not list_directory, not anything). Do not describe your reply or explain that no tool is needed -- just say the thing a person would say. The same applies to a message that doesn't read like a real request at all -- a fragment, a stray word, or something that looks garbled (voice input sometimes mishears words) -- ask what he meant or say you didn't catch that, instead of guessing a tool call for it (e.g. calling get_news with nonsense as the 'topic'). Only reach for a tool once the message actually reads like a coherent request for something. Every tool call costs real time the person is sitting there waiting through, so skip it whenever a direct answer is possible. You also have a skills library -- specific how-to guides for particular kinds of tasks. Call 'list_skills' to see what's available, and 'read_skill' to load one BEFORE attempting a task it covers (e.g. organizing files, giving a daily briefing, taking notes) -- follow its instructions rather than improvising. A tool result is ground truth: report exactly what it says, including errors and 'User declined' messages. Never invent or guess at a command's output, a file's contents, or any other tool result -- if a tool failed or was declined, say so plainly instead of describing what it would have returned. If a tool call errors because you got the arguments wrong (e.g. a function that takes no arguments got one anyway), just call it again correctly -- do not present your own guess at what it would have said as if it were the real result.

tools._about: The tools the model is offered, in this order: name, description and JSON-schema parameters, wrapped in Ollama's function envelope by brain._tool_definitions. Every tool here must be a function in tools.py (scripts/test_tool_policy.py checks) and have a tool_policy.json entry saying what a call may do. All of a tool's guidance -- when to use it, what to say about its result -- belongs in its description, never in the prompt (see prompt._about): the description is in context only on the turns tool_router offers the tool, so no other turn pays for it. enabled_env (optional): the definition is left out while that environment variable is 0/false/off/no. _note keys record why a tool is worded as it is.

definitions.name: run_shell_command
definitions.description: Run a shell command on the local machine and return its output. Never a command that deletes, moves, renames or overwrites his files or folders ('delete my downloads folder', 'clear out my desktop'): you don't do that, even when asked, because it can't be undone and nothing brings the files back. Don't call this for such a request -- tell him you won't, say why (it's permanent), and that he can do it himself or use the Recycle Bin.

definitions.name: open_application
definitions.description: Open an installed app by name, or open an existing document using its full path. For a file, CV or resume, first use find_files to get the real full path; then pass that path here. Finding or reading a file does not open it on screen.

app_name.description: Name or path of the application to open.

definitions.name: list_directory
definitions.description: List files and folders at a given path.

path.description: Directory path to list. Defaults to current directory.

definitions.name: find_files
definitions.description: Find/locate a file by name when the user doesn't know or give an exact path -- searches recursively through their common folders (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Videos, Music, GitHub, OneDrive) and returns matching full paths, newest first. Use this instead of list_directory when the user is asking you to find or locate something rather than browse a folder they already named.

query.description: Filename or part of a filename to search for, e.g. 'invoice' or '*.pdf'.

location.description: Optional: narrow the search to one folder, e.g. 'downloads' or 'desktop'. Leave empty to search everywhere.

definitions.name: read_file
definitions.description: Read the text contents of a file -- only when he asks what a file says. 'Where is', 'find' and 'open' never need this; a found file's name and folder is the answer to 'where'.

path.description: Path to the file to read.

definitions.name: write_file
definitions.description: Write text content to one of HIS files, overwriting it if it already exists. Never your own files: your settings, config, code and memory are his to edit, not yours, and a write to any of them is refused -- so if he asks you to edit your own settings or config, don't call this at all; tell him plainly you don't change your own files and he can edit them himself.

path.description: Path to the file to write.

definitions.name: get_current_time
definitions._note: Leave this description alone: get_current_time is core, so every turn pays for it. A paragraph listing the non-time turns cost the garbled case 2/6 against 6/6, and one added sentence moved 'ha, do that again' (A/B, 2026-11-04). The clock reflex is handled before the model instead (quick_replies.never_mind) and by routing the right tools.
definitions.description: Get the current date and time -- this machine's own local time, or, given a timezone, the current time somewhere else instead.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name for elsewhere, e.g. 'Asia/Tokyo', 'Asia/Hong_Kong', 'America/New_York'. Omit for this machine's own local time.

definitions.name: calculate
definitions.description: Evaluate a math expression exactly -- always use this for arithmetic instead of computing it yourself, even for something that looks simple, since that's exactly where a mental slip happens. Supports + - * / // % ** parentheses, unary minus, constants pi/e, and sqrt/abs/round/sin/cos/tan/log/log10/log2/exp/floor/ceil/factorial/pow/min/max. Translate a word problem or percentage into a plain expression first, e.g. '15% of 240' -> '240 * 0.15'.

expression.description: A plain math expression, e.g. '(17 + 3) * 4' or '240 * 0.15' or 'sqrt(144)'.

definitions.name: get_weather
definitions.description: Get a short current-weather summary for a place.

definitions.name: get_news
definitions.description: Get the latest real headlines from CNA (Channel NewsAsia). Use this for any news/current-events question -- never guess or make up headlines. It always returns real headlines, even with no topic given -- an empty topic is normal and valid, not an error, and just means general top headlines. Your reply MUST actually name at least 2-3 of the specific real headlines/topics it returned, in your own words -- a reply like 'I've got the news for you' with no actual content is wrong and useless, exactly as wrong as saying you couldn't find any.

topic.description: Optional topic/category to filter by, e.g. 'business', 'singapore', 'world'. Leave empty for general top headlines -- do not ask the user for a topic first, just call it.

definitions.name: play_song
definitions.description: Search Spotify for a track and start playing it. Needs Spotify set up (SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID/SECRET) and the Spotify app already open on this machine -- if the result says no active device, tell the user to open Spotify first (or call open_application('Spotify') yourself, then retry). Not configured at all yet is a normal, expected state to report plainly, not an error to apologize for.

query.description: Song name, optionally with artist, e.g. 'Heart Shaker Twice' or 'Blinding Lights The Weeknd'.

definitions.name: pause_music
definitions.description: Pause whatever is currently playing on Spotify.

definitions.name: resume_music
definitions.description: Resume Spotify playback after a pause.

definitions.name: skip_song
definitions.description: Skip to the next track on Spotify.

definitions.name: previous_song
definitions.description: Go back to the previous track on Spotify.

definitions.name: current_track
definitions.description: Check what's currently playing on Spotify (song, artist, playing/paused) -- call this instead of guessing if asked what's playing.

definitions.name: get_voice_settings
definitions.description: Check what voice is actually speaking your replies out loud right now. You have no built-in knowledge of this -- call this instead of guessing if asked about your own voice.

definitions.name: get_brain_location
definitions.description: Check your actual code/memory paths, editable brain rules and current learning status. Use when asked about your brain, rules or whether you are learning; never guess these settings.

definitions.name: look_at_this
definitions.description: Read what Chuen is pointing at: the text selected in the window he's using (or, if nothing is selected, his clipboard), plus that window's title. Use for 'explain this', 'rewrite this shorter', 'what does this error mean', 'translate this' when he hasn't pasted the text himself. Not for files on disk.

definitions.name: get_system_status
definitions.description: Check the laptop's current disk space, memory, and CPU usage.

definitions.name: clean_temp_files
definitions.description: Delete old (24h+ untouched) temp files to free disk space. This already runs automatically every hour in the background -- use this to trigger it on demand.

definitions.name: list_startup_programs
definitions.description: List programs configured to launch automatically at login.

definitions.name: disable_startup_program
definitions.description: Stop a program from launching at login (reversible with restore_startup_program). See list_startup_programs for valid names.

name.description: Program name as shown by list_startup_programs.

definitions.name: restore_startup_program
definitions.description: Undo a previous disable_startup_program call, restoring that program to launch at login again.

definitions.name: remember
definitions.description: Save a fact about the user for later recall, e.g. remember('favorite_coffee', 'flat white').

key.description: Short identifier for the fact, e.g. 'favorite_coffee'.

definitions.name: recall
definitions.description: Recall a previously remembered fact about the user by its key.

key.description: The identifier used when the fact was saved.

definitions.name: list_known_facts
definitions.description: List every fact currently remembered about the user.

definitions.name: list_skills
definitions.description: List available skills (how-to guides for specific kinds of tasks).

definitions.name: read_skill
definitions.description: Read the full instructions for one skill by name (see list_skills).

definitions.name: add_task
definitions.description: Add something Chuen has to do, optionally with a deadline. Use this whenever he says he needs to do something by a time -- 'remind me to email Sunway before Friday' is add_task('email Sunway', 'before Friday'). Pass his own words for the deadline; don't work out the date yourself. If he gave a time but not what the reminder is FOR ('remind me thursday'), don't add anything -- ask him what it's for in one short question. If the result says the time is ambiguous, ask him that question instead.

text.description: What needs doing, e.g. 'email Sunway about the firm visit'.

due.description: The deadline, copied from his words -- 'before Friday', 'tomorrow 5pm', 'on the 6th of October 14:00'. If the date is part of the sentence, put it here AS WELL as leaving it in the text. Omit only when he gave no time at all.

definitions.name: list_tasks
definitions.description: Read out Chuen's open tasks. Use this for ANY question about what he has to do or where his tasks are -- 'what's on my plate', 'what do I have to do', 'where is the task list', 'show me my tasks', 'anything due'. Then tell him what the result actually says: name each task and its deadline. Never answer a question about his tasks from memory, and never say the list 'is there' without reading it. If he asks WHERE the list is, answer by telling him what is on it -- do not state a file path or filename; you do not know where it is stored and will get it wrong.

definitions.name: complete_task
definitions.description: Mark a task done once Chuen says he's finished it. Describe the task in words -- it's matched on those. If more than one matches it refuses rather than guessing, so pass enough to be specific.

task.description: Words identifying the task, e.g. 'the Sunway email'.

definitions.name: remove_task
definitions.description: Delete a task that was added by mistake. For tasks he has actually done, use complete_task instead so the record is kept.

task.description: Words identifying the task to delete.

definitions.name: set_timer
definitions._note: Timers (timers.py), added 2026-10-20 after 'start timer' was answered with run_shell_command('start') and 'The timer has started.' All the guidance is in these descriptions, not the prompt; tool_router only offers them when the message is about a timer.
definitions.description: Start a countdown timer that pings Chuen from the orb when it ends. Use for 'start a timer', 'set a timer for 10 minutes', 'remind me in 5 minutes to check the oven', 'time me for 30 seconds'. This is the ONLY way to start a timer -- never use run_shell_command or open_application for one. If he didn't say how long, call it with no length and it will tell you to ask him. Not for the pomodoro study timer, and not for a deadline days away (add_task).

seconds.description: Extra seconds, or the whole length for a short timer.

label.description: What it's for, in a few words, e.g. 'oven'. Optional.

duration.description: Or the length in his own words, e.g. '20 mins', 'an hour and a half' -- used when minutes/seconds aren't given.

definitions.name: cancel_timer
definitions.description: Stop a running countdown timer: 'stop the timer', 'cancel the oven timer'. Report exactly what it returns -- if it says no timer was running, say that.

label.description: Which timer, if he named one. Leave out to stop the running one.

definitions.name: list_timers
definitions.description: How long is left on running timers: 'how long is left on my timer?'.

definitions.name: study_session_status
definitions._note: Study mode (study_mode.py), model-visible since 2026-11-03: before, the pomodoro ran only on a whole-message phrase match, so 'is the study session running?' went to list_directory and 'pause sutuy timer' paused Spotify. Offered by the 'study' group (tool_policy.json), whose cues include 'timer' and 'session' so a typo'd 'sutuy timer' still gets them.
definitions.description: Whether a study session (the 25-minute study / 5-minute rest pomodoro) is running, paused or off, and how long is left. Use for 'is the study session running?', 'how long left on my study timer?'. It is not a plain countdown timer (list_timers) and not a file or folder.

definitions.name: start_study_session
definitions.description: Start a study session: 25 minutes of study, then a 5-minute rest, round and round, with a countdown pill and a message at each switch. For 'start a study session', 'pomodoro', 'study timer' -- including misspellings. Not for a plain countdown ('10 minute timer' is set_timer).

definitions.name: pause_study_session
definitions.description: Pause the running study session where it is; the countdown freezes until resume_study_session. 'pause the study timer', 'hold the session'. Report exactly what it returns -- if it says nothing was running, say that.

definitions.name: resume_study_session
definitions.description: Continue a paused study session from where it was paused: 'resume', 'carry on', 'ok go on', 'back to it', 'unpause' while the session is paused. Not Spotify (resume_music) and not a new session (start_study_session). Report exactly what it returns.

definitions.name: stop_study_session
definitions.description: End the study session for good: 'stop the study session', 'session over', 'I'm done studying', 'end pomodoro'. Report exactly what it returns -- if it says no session was running, say that plainly (no goodbye, no clock).

definitions.name: check_calendar
definitions._note: Nothing is connected to a calendar, and the model asserted an empty one for 'what's on my calendar tomorrow?' (2026-11-04, 2/6). A tool result is the one thing it treats as ground truth, so the fact that there is no calendar to read is a tool (tools.check_calendar); its reply_must_mention net is policy.
definitions.description: What is on Chuen's calendar for a day: 'what's on my calendar tomorrow?', 'am I free Thursday?', 'any meetings today?'. Call it rather than answering from memory -- you have no idea what is on his calendar unless this says. If it says no calendar is connected, tell him you can't see his calendar; never say it's empty or that he is free. His reminders are list_tasks.

day.description: The day he asked about, in his words: 'tomorrow', 'Thursday'. Optional.

definitions.name: reply_preference
definitions._note: How he wants her to talk -- a standing instruction, never a task. On 2026-10-31 'don't show me the file path, ask next time' became the task 'ask for file path next time'. See reply_preferences.py.
definitions.description: Save a standing instruction from Chuen about HOW you should reply from now on -- 'don't read out file paths, ask if I want them', 'keep it short', 'say me instead of Chuen', 'no need to repeat the whole message'. It is remembered and followed in every later reply. This is never a task or reminder (add_task is for things HE has to do) and never a file to write. action 'remove' drops one he no longer wants; 'list' shows them.

text.description: The instruction, in his words, e.g. 'don't show the file path, ask first'.

definitions.name: search_vault
definitions._note: Second attempt at letting Denisse see the Obsidian vault. The first pasted Dev/Memory/ into the system prompt and measured 0/4 clean against 4/4 with it off. This one is a tool she calls, so an unrelated question pays only for this description. enabled_env: the tool is left out while DENISSE_VAULT_SEARCH is 0/false/off/no -- the control arm, so the A/B can be re-run.
definitions.description: Search Chuen's own Obsidian notes and quote them. Use this for a question about HIS material and HIS history -- his modules, lectures, tutorials and deadlines, what was decided about Denisse and why, how his machine is set up. For a current-project overview use query 'current projects'. For his societies, 'when is the CM coursework due', 'who lectures electromagnetism', 'what did we decide about the reminder card', 'what is convolution again' all belong here, because his notes have his answer rather than a general one. Do NOT use it for general knowledge, for anything about the current moment (time, weather, news), or for his task list -- list_tasks owns that. Report only what the result actually quotes; if it says nothing in the notes matches, say exactly that instead of filling the gap from your own guess.

query.description: The subject to look up, in a few words -- 'computational methods coursework deadline', 'reminder card decision'. Keywords, not a sentence.

definitions.name: tutor_explain
definitions._note: The study tutor (tutor/, part 3, 2026-11-05). Its name is tutor.json 'name'; every result opens with it introducing itself, and tool_policy.json reply_must_mention keeps that in her reply. Hard topics and a local answer that fails its own check go to Claude in the background (delegate.py), so the result may be 'asked Claude; it will pop up'.
definitions.description: Have the study tutor explain a topic from one of Chuen's university modules, step by step, from his own lecture notes and tutor notes -- 'explain convolution', 'teach me the Laplace transform', 'I don't get Gauss's law', 'go over the card I got wrong on impedance'. The result is the tutor's lesson plus one check question for him; put the lesson to him in the tutor's name and ask the check question, keeping the model answer back until he tries. If the result says the topic was sent to Claude, say that and that it will pop up. Not for general knowledge outside his modules, and not a search (search_vault quotes notes; this teaches).

topic.description: The topic in a few words, as he said it: 'convolution', 'Laplace transform', 'Gauss's law'.

module.description: The module, if he named one: its name, code or short form ('signals', 'EM', '5CCYB020'). Leave empty when he didn't; the tutor works it out or asks.

definitions.name: tutor_quiz
definitions.description: Quiz Chuen on a module from the study tutor's revision cards -- 'quiz me on signals', 'test me on EM', 'give me five questions on Fourier', or the end-of-round check study mode offers. Returns numbered questions, weakest topics first; the tutor keeps the answers. Put the questions to him in the tutor's name; when he answers, call tutor_mark_answer with what he wrote. If it says there are no cards yet, tell him how to make them (the result says).

module.description: The module: name, code or short form ('signals', 'EM'). Empty if he didn't say; the tutor asks.

topic.description: Narrow to one topic, if he named one ('Fourier'). Optional.

count.description: How many questions, if he said. Optional; the tutor's default otherwise.

definitions.name: tutor_weak_topics
definitions.description: What Chuen keeps getting wrong in a module, measured from his Anki reviews of the tutor's cards (lapses, ease, what is due) and the learner model -- 'what's weak in EM?', 'what should I revise for signals?', 'where am I struggling?'. Tell him the topics and which week's notes to revise, in the tutor's name. If it says there are no review stats yet, say exactly that; never guess what is weak.

module.description: The module: name, code or short form ('signals', 'EM'). Empty if he didn't say.

definitions.name: tutor_exam_question
definitions.description: Set Chuen a longer exam-style problem on a module, in the style of his coursework and past papers, worth marks, with several parts -- 'give me an exam question', 'exam practice on signals', 'a past-paper style question on Laplace'. The tutor keeps the mark scheme. Give him the whole problem in the tutor's name; when he answers, call tutor_mark_answer with his whole answer. Takes a moment: it is written by the local model from his notes.

module.description: The module: name, code or short form. Empty if he didn't say.

topic.description: The topic to set it on, if he named one. Optional.

definitions.name: tutor_mark_answer
definitions.description: Mark Chuen's answer to the question the study tutor last set him (a quiz or an exam-style problem) -- call it when he answers after a tutor_quiz or tutor_exam_question, or says 'mark this', 'here's my answer', 'check my working'. Quiz answers are marked against the cards straight away; an exam answer goes to Claude with the mark scheme and the result pops up later -- say so. Report the marks and the feedback on each step in the tutor's name. Pass his answer exactly as he wrote it.

answer.description: His answer, verbatim -- all of it, numbering kept.

module.description: The module, if he named one. Empty: the question set last.

style_examples._about: Made-up exchanges in her voice, placed between the system prompt and the real conversation (2026-10-22: she talked in report-voice, and the model copies the conversation it is shown). Tool results use the real formats so the examples look like her own turns. No prompt here may match an eval case, or the suite measures recall of the example. Switched by style_examples in memory/brain_rules.json or DENISSE_STYLE_EXAMPLES.

messages.content: Here are a few made-up example exchanges showing how you sound. They never happened -- never mention them. The real conversation follows.
remind me to email Ben friday at 5
Got it -- I'll remind you to email Ben on Friday at 5.
Dogs, probably. Cats do have the better attitude though. You?

json_leak._about: A reply that is really a JSON status object (2026-09-23: '{"status": "success", ...}' to a tick-off). fields: the first of these holding text is said instead; else the last tool result; else fallback.

reply_nets._about: Nets under the model's reply. tool_narration: a reply made ENTIRELY of commentary on her own tool use ('No tool call needed for that.'); one retry with plain_reply_nudge. tool_talk: narration wrapped round a real answer ('I called the get_weather tool...'); any tool name containing _ counts too. tool_lead_in: lead-ins cut from the front of such a sentence; if fewer than min_words_kept survive the cut, the original stands. didnt_catch: 'I didn't catch that' to a message of at least clear_message_min_words words (word_pattern) gets one retry without the history. role_prefix: the chat template's role marker emitted as text ('assistant\n\nNo worries.'), lowercase as observed.
reply_nets.plain_reply_nudge: Your last draft talked about tools instead of answering. Reply to his last message the way a person would, in a few words, and don't mention tools or functions.

weather._about: follow_up_place_pattern: 'and in Penang?' after a weather question -- group 1 is the place, fetched by the code (live the model answered from memory 3/3). A place that is one of not_a_place or has a time word (tool_policy.json cue time_words) is not a place. data_patterns: weather DATA words that mean the reply invented a forecast when get_weather never ran; line_patterns: the sentences then dropped; not_checked: said when nothing is left.
weather.not_checked: I haven't checked the weather -- ask me and I'll look it up.

paths._about: His standing asks of 2026-10-31: no file paths read out. windows_path_pattern (case-sensitive; named group 'name' is the file or folder name) finds the paths in a reply; each becomes its name, then ask is appended once, and the full paths are kept for a yes_pattern answer (max_shown of them). wants_path_patterns: he asked for the path, so it is kept. search_miss_pattern -> search_miss_replacement shortens find_files' 'No files matching ... found in <folders>' line. any_path_pattern: any Windows path in text, for the file-reply checks.
paths.search_miss_pattern: (No files matching '[^']*' found) in [^.\n]*\.(?: That only covers the folders searched\.)?

second_person._about: Notes say '<name> is a collaborator'; she reads that out to him, so his name becomes 'you' (the name is settings.user_name()'s first word). verbs: the verb after his name and its second-person form. possessive_not_before: "<name>'s" stays when one of these follows ("Chuen's is" is not possessive). verb_cues: words after the name that mark it as the subject. address_lead_ins: 'Hey Chuen' and 'Thanks, Chuen' are talking to him already and stay. possessive_replacement: what "<name>'s" becomes. pronouns: swapped in a sentence that changed; subject_pronoun likewise, with verbs. capitalise: these words are capitalised at the start of a sentence.

notes._about: header_pattern (multiline): vault_search's dated-context header, said as header_replacement. asks_due_pattern: he asked about a deadline, so a due year in the notes is kept (specify_year). found: said over a reply that denies vault access when the notes were read. say: a retry that still says it found nothing is replaced by the notes themselves. appended_to_result: joins a find_files miss (or a stale recall) to what the notes say, as the model reads it. due_year_pattern: a deadline's year in the notes (group 1), kept with specify_year when the reply (year_pattern, as written) has no year.
notes.found: I can search your vault. Here's what I found:

dates._about: A deadline he never said: 'remind me to submit the team sign up' became 'on the 6th of October at 2 PM' (2026-10-31). due_words (whole numbers always count) are the words that pin a date; every one in the model's due has to be in his message, after due_aliases, except always_allowed.

tasks._about: deadline_only_pattern: 'before 2nd of november' said right after she added a task sets that task's deadline, if the task is under move_window_minutes old and her last reply named its first move_match_chars characters. moved: the reply. The task tools' results are said in her words (added_*, completed, removed; the store's date, never the model's). content_word_pattern / content_stop_words / min_shared_words: a reply after list_tasks must use the list's words or the list is said instead.
tasks.added_no_deadline: Got it -- I added "{text}", no deadline.

news._about: A news reply with no news in it ('I've got the latest news for you.') while get_news returned headlines: the net reads max_headlines of them out. head_pattern: the result's lead-in before the list. strip_prefix_pattern: cut from a headline. A reply counts as relaying the news when it shares min_shared_words words (word_pattern) with the headlines.

honesty._about: A reply that says something was DONE (learning.json claims_done) with no tool this turn confirming it. Nudges go back round the loop once, this call only: no_tool_claim when nothing ran, wrong_tool_claim ({ran}) when what ran can't do that, unconfirmed_claim ({results}) otherwise. Still unsupported: failed_reply over nothing but errors, else unconfirmed_reply. claim_needs: a done-claim matching pattern also needs one of its tools to have run. set_for: 'Timer set for 5 minutes' counts as a done-claim. delete_claim_pattern: files said to be gone, done-word or not, unless negated_before_pattern ends the negation_window_chars before it; delete_tools are the only tools that remove anything. state_tools: their result is the one true account; a reply contradicting it is replaced by the result up to result_cut_markers.
honesty.no_tool_claim_nudge: You just said it was done, but you didn't call any tool this turn, so nothing actually happened. If one of your tools does what he asked, call it now. If none does, tell him plainly that you can't do that yet -- don't say it's done.
honesty.unconfirmed_claim_nudge: You just said it worked, but no tool this turn confirmed that anything happened -- they returned: {results}. Don't say it worked. Either call the tool that actually does what he asked, or tell him plainly what happened.
honesty.wrong_tool_claim_nudge: You just said it was done, but the only tools that ran this turn were {ran}, and none of them does that. Call the tool that actually does what he asked now, or tell him plainly it isn't done.
honesty.unconfirmed_reply: I haven't confirmed that action, so I can't say it's done.

evidence._about: A tool result that is no evidence the thing was done: empty or one of empty_results, a learning.json tool failure, one of no_evidence_prefixes, or no_evidence_pattern. found_nothing_patterns: a lookup's own words for finding nothing (matched at the start). recovery_sources: where else a lookup that found nothing is checked, read-only, one step. lookup_filler: words dropped from his request when working out what he was looking for (word_pattern finds the words). says_nothing_patterns: a retry still saying it found nothing when the notes were seeded.

lookup._about: Nothing found anywhere: where she looked, per tool, then one question (blocked, with {where} and {terms}). where: per tool, nothing ({terms}) or, when unreachable_pattern matches the result, unreachable. nowhere: when no tool ran. fallback_terms: the subject when his words gave none.

where.nothing: none of your saved facts covers it

lookup.nowhere: I had nowhere else to look
lookup.blocked: I checked again: {where}. I haven't found it, and I won't guess. What did you file it under -- a note title or a word in it?

clock._about: The current date or time said with no clock run ('It's currently December 2023.' -- her training cutoff as today). A bare number only counts with a clock shape; a day or month only when says_now or says_today precedes it. The sentence is replaced by real_time.

cues._about: Requests the code answers before the model, because the eval showed the model wrong 3 runs out of 3 (2026-10-29), each matched against his whole message. news_off: switch the daily briefing off (not a news request). self_model: what she runs on is a fact (model_config). briefing / plan_study: planner.py's jobs. watchlist_*: invest.py, no model. study_brief: one module's brief from his notes (study_brief.py); the *_with_module patterns need a module name (module_names, mirroring study_brief.json's aliases) later in the sentence. follow_on: 'go on, do that one' -- the job is the turn before's (carry_*). plan_yes: accepting a planner offer (planner_offer_marker in her last reply). ack: a bare acknowledgement, skipped when looking for the request a complaint is about. delegate / keep_local: writing, research and solutions go to Claude (delegate.py) unless the request is local and checkable. done_word: a complaint about 'Done'. style_note_excludes: a reply preference (tool_policy.json cue reply_preference) that is really a reminder. vault_queries: his internships and projects live in the vault; a request matching every pattern in all_of_patterns searches for query. vault_overview_query: what search_vault is asked for when he wants the overview (instincts.wants_vault_overview). verify_claim_pattern: a yes/no about her last action ('did you open it?'), answered from the evidence; promise_pattern: her reply promised it ('Opening it now'), so nothing recorded means it didn't happen.
cues.promise_pattern: \b(?:\w+ing (?:it|that|them|this|one|the \w+) now|on it|will do|right away|one sec(?:ond)?|just a (?:sec|moment|minute))\b

quick_replies._about: Greetings and acknowledgements have one right kind of answer and the model kept finding wrong ones ('hey' -> 'No response needed.'), so they are answered before the model. {name} is settings.user_name()'s first word. day_part_pattern: a greeting that names the time of day gets greeting_by_time with the first day_parts entry whose until_hour is after now. An 'ok' or 'thanks' right after a question of hers is an answer and goes to the model. never_mind_pattern -> never_mind: 'nvm' drops the thing, mid-question or not (the clock was called first 8/8 otherwise).

file_query._about: What to search for when she answered a file request without searching: only from 'my <thing>' or 'called/named <thing>' (named_patterns, first match wins, group 1 is the thing), never from a whole sentence. A message with a path (path_pattern) is left alone. stop_words are dropped and at most max_words kept (word_pattern finds them).

skills._about: list_skills ran and the reply was 'I've got a few skills that might come in handy' (3/3): the list is said instead unless the reply names one. A name's words of at least min_word_chars letters count, except generic_words ('take' from take_notes matched 'I can take care of it'). heading and line are the restored reply; strip_prefix_pattern is cut from each description.
skills.heading: Here's what I can help with:

text._about: Her fixed replies. news_off: after switching the briefing off. identity_sized / identity_plain: what she runs on ({family} {n} from the model tag, or {model}). noted / noted_unsaved: a reply preference taken. you_asked: prefix on every complaint repair ({shown} is his request, clipped). already_done ({what}): the complained-about action already happened. same_answer ({retry}): the retry repeated the rejected answer. feedback_commands: typed commands and their replies. done_complaint: a complaint about 'Done'. gave_up: the tool loop ran out. matching_files + matching_files_shown: appended when a search found files the reply didn't name. no_verified_results / only_searched_folders / lookup_incomplete: file replies corrected against what find_files actually returned. paths_shown: how the full paths are listed. corrected ({retry}): the complaint repair changed the answer, so the first one was wrong. verified_done / verified_failed ({what}) / verified_nothing: 'did you open it?' answered from the last attempt's evidence. not_one_found: the item he named when asked which one isn't among those found.
text.news_off: Okay, no more daily news -- I've switched the briefing off. Ask me whenever you do want the headlines.
text.identity_sized: I'm {family} {n}B -- about {n} billion parameters, running locally on your laptop through Ollama.
text.identity_plain: I'm {model}, running locally on your laptop through Ollama.
text.noted_unsaved: Alright, noted -- though I couldn't save it, so remind me if I slip.
text.already_done: That part is already done ({what}), and I haven't done it again. What did you want instead?
text.same_answer: I got the same answer again, so I haven't fixed it: {retry} Tell me what you meant and I'll do that instead.
text.verified_nothing: No -- I said I would, but I didn't actually do it; nothing ran for that. Want me to do it now?

feedback_commands.reply: Thanks — that tells me the last answer was helpful.
Got it — the last answer was wrong. Tell me what should happen instead.

text.done_complaint: I shouldn't have said 'Done' without verifying it. The last action is unverified.
text.gave_up: I got stuck working that one out -- could you rephrase it?
text.no_verified_results: I don't have verified file-search results for that request yet.
text.only_searched_folders: That only covers the folders searched.
text.lookup_incomplete: I couldn't complete the file lookup, so I can't tell whether it's there.

nudges._about: System notes added to one model call only, never to the stored history. rejected_answer ({wrong}): a read found something and he said the answer was wrong. clarified_answer ({spoken}, {evidence}): answer from the one item he picked.
nudges.rejected_answer: He said your answer "{wrong}" was not what he asked. Use the results above. If more than one thing in them could be what he means, ask which one in one short question. Don't repeat that answer.
nudges.clarified_answer:
He means {spoken}. From his notes: {evidence}
Answer his question from this alone, in one or two sentences. Don't add anything it doesn't say.

tool_errors._about: What a tool call gets back from the code instead of the tool, as the model reads it ({name} is the tool). The opening words are read by other modules and must stay: multistep.py treats 'User declined' and "Refused: this exact '" as a step that failed and strips "Error running '<tool>':" / 'Refused:' when saying a result to Chuen; learning.json's tool_failure patterns match 'Error' and 'Refused'. already_ran: a once_per_turn tool (tool_policy.json) called twice -- told to tick off one task, the model closed an unrelated one too, 3/3 (2026-09-23). missing_argument ({missing}): the raw TypeError told the model the call failed but not how to fix it, so it reported the thing as not found. failed ({error}): the model's instinct on a tool error is to invent a plausible result. last_round: the tool loop's final round, tools withheld. not_offered: a tool that changes something, called when the router didn't offer it. step_repeated / retry_repeated: the same call again within a plan step, or after he said the answer was wrong (naming alternatives here was tried live 2026-10-30: 0/5, ~2x slower).
tool_errors.already_ran: Refused: '{name}' has already run once this turn. Only act on the one thing Chuen actually named. If he meant something else too, ask him.
tool_errors.missing_argument: Error running '{name}': no value was given for the required argument '{missing}'. Call '{name}' again with {missing}=<value>. Do not invent a result.
tool_errors.failed: Error running '{name}': {error}. Tell the user this failed. Do not invent a result.
tool_errors.last_round: Refused: no more tool calls this turn. Answer him in words from what you already have.
tool_errors.no_such_tool: Refused: there is no tool called '{name}'. Use one of the tools you were given, or answer directly.
tool_errors.not_offered: Refused: '{name}' isn't available for this request. Answer the user's actual request.
tool_errors.step_repeated: Refused: this exact '{name}' call was already made for this step. Do it a different way, or tell him plainly what you couldn't do.
tool_errors.retry_repeated: Refused: this exact '{name}' call already failed and he said the answer was wrong. Do something different, or tell him plainly what you can't do.

startup._about: What Brain() raises when it can't start, shown by the tray. ollama_unreachable takes {error}; model_missing takes {model}.
startup.ollama_unreachable: Can't reach the local Ollama server: {error}. Make sure Ollama is installed and running (it should start automatically -- check for its icon in the system tray).
startup.model_missing: Model '{model}' isn't downloaded yet. Run: ollama pull {model}

memory._about: explicit_request_pattern: an instruction to retain a fact ('remember that...', 'save this as a fact', 'keep in mind'), not a question asking for recall ('remember what I said?'). While save_facts is 'explicit' (memory/brain_rules.json), the remember tool is offered only on a message matching this (tool_router.select via brain_rules.explicit_memory_request). It is a phrase match standing in for understanding him; dropping it would offer remember on every turn, which is an A/B to run, not a data edit.

settings._about: His editable settings file (brain_rules.py): file is its path under the program folder (DENISSE_RULES_FILE overrides), read up to max_file_bytes. defaults are the values when the file is missing or invalid and the template for brain_rules.example.json; ranges are [low, high] for each whole-number setting; save_facts_values are the allowed save_facts words.
